texts.title: When does failure teach?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall the last mistake you made… and keep it in mind.
texts.hook.h2: They say: failure is the first step to success… really?
texts.hook.h3: I gave the same presentation twice… and made the same mistake.
texts.hook.h4: 53 studies asked: try to solve it first… or hear the explanation first?
texts.hook.h5.frame: Ask why… or just move on?
texts.hook.h5: When something doesn't work at your job… do you ask why? Or just move on?
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour. Her presentation didn't work.
texts.s1.l1: No big deal… failure is the first step to success!
texts.s1.l2: I saw the presentation… want my opinion?
texts.s1.l3: No… I'll present it as it is.
texts.s1.a2: And you… did you find where your mistake was?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time Nour will ask about her mistake.
texts.s1.l4: I saw the presentation… want my opinion?
texts.s1.l6: Too many numbers… I got lost myself.
texts.s1.l7: One idea per slide… not perfect, but clearer.
texts.book.card: To get better you must fail… there's no other way.
texts.book.l1: The book says: there's no progress without falls… so look for them, and learn from them.
texts.book.l2: Like cooking: every dish you ruin… teaches you something.
texts.verdict.card: 53 studies · those who tried before the explanation understood better
texts.verdict.nuance: But someone who tries alone, with no explanation? Often learns less.
texts.verdict.l2: 53 studies: students tried to solve it before the lesson, most couldn't… and after the explanation, they understood better.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Nour: after a mistake, ask « what didn't work? » before trying again. It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone who always says « failure is the first step to success ».
